s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic abdominal pain and diarrhea with gastrointestinal mucosal inflammation and granulomatous changes
salient_findings: Abdominal pain and three loose, watery stools daily for 1.5 years
Erythematous mucosa and congestion in the colon, terminal ileum, and stomach
Non-caseating microgranulomas in biopsies from the stomach, duodenum, terminal ileum, colon, and rectum
key_facts: Hereditary hemochromatosis (grade 3 iron overload, mild portal fibrosis, C282Y homozygosity)
Negative ova and parasites, bacterial culture, fecal leukocytes, and Clostridium difficile NAAT
Negative Histoplasma antigen, anti-transglutaminase, and anti-endomysial antibodies
Hepatosplenomegaly on CT of the abdomen and pelvis

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level and non-caseating microgranulomas on biopsy

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and gastrointestinal mucosal inflammation with granulomatous changes

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation and presence of hepatosplenomegaly

shortlist.label: Idiopathic granulomatous gastritis
shortlist.why_kept: Non-caseating microgranulomas on gastric biopsy and absence of other explanatory conditions

shortlist.label: Blau syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Combination of granulomatous inflammation, gastrointestinal involvement, and presence of hepatosplenomegaly

raw.rationale: The presence of non-caseating microgranulomas in biopsies from multiple sites, elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level, and hepatosplenomegaly are consistent with sarcoidosis, which can cause gastrointestinal and systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: While Crohn's disease can cause abdominal pain, diarrhea, and gastrointestinal inflammation, the presence of non-caseating microgranulomas and elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme level are more suggestive of sarcoidosis.
